question: Should this repository accept the proposed `externalResolution` and `plugin.approval.resolveVerified` approval boundary after proof/status updates, or keep the RFC in draft until the linked host API and AgentKit reference flow are proven?
rationale: The PR is a coherent RFC draft, but accepting it would bless a compatibility-sensitive plugin API and approval security boundary that automation cannot decide for maintainers.

options.title: Keep Draft Until Gates Clear
options.body: Require maintainer agreement on resolver authority, grant semantics, audit fields, channel fallback, and direct redacted proof before accepting the RFC.

options.title: Accept With Explicit Deferrals
options.body: Accept the RFC only if unresolved implementation choices are written as bounded deferrals that do not imply approval of security-boundary behavior.

options.title: Narrow Or Pause The RFC
options.body: Ask the author to narrow the host API further or pause the draft if maintainers are not ready to sponsor this plugin approval direction.

recommendation.title: Keep Draft Until Gates Clear
recommendation.body: Require maintainer agreement on resolver authority, grant semantics, audit fields, channel fallback, and direct redacted proof before accepting the RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: kevinslin owns the visible current RFC-review thread and authored the lifecycle guidance that gates draft acceptance.
